summary: Frontend-only validation of the PushSubscribeButton fix on homepage '/'. Baseline render, permission=default click flow (stubbed granted & denied), granted-upfront render branch, and homepage regression smoke were tested with Playwright. Button is now fully functional (state transitions correct), but the GRANTED path shows the wrong (error) toast because window.webpushr('subscribe') throws and is caught by the generic catch block before toast.success() runs.

ui_bugs.issue: On successful grant the user sees the FAILURE toast 'Notification permission nahi mil paayi. Dobara try karein.' instead of the success toast, while the UI simultaneously flips to 'Push Alerts ON ✓' — contradictory feedback. Cause: window.webpushr('subscribe') throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading apply)' (placeholder Webpushr key, SDK not initialised) and the whole block is inside one try/catch, so the throw happens BEFORE toast.success(). Fix: wrap the webpushr handoff in its own try/catch (or check typeof window.webpushr === 'function' && window.webpushr.q/init state) and always show the success toast when result === 'granted'.

action_items: PushSubscribeButton.jsx: isolate the Webpushr handoff (document.getElementById('webpushr-subscription-button').click() / window.webpushr('subscribe')) in its own try/catch so a Webpushr SDK exception cannot suppress the success toast on granted permission.
critical_code_review_comments: subscribe(): single try/catch spans both the permission request and the third-party SDK call; a third-party failure is reported to the user as a permission failure. Separate the concerns.
The 2s setInterval polling of Notification.permission is acceptable but consider navigator.permissions.query({name:'notifications'}).onchange to avoid a permanent timer.

success_rate.frontend: 80% (4/5 scenarios fully pass; granted-path toast wrong)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified scenarios: (1) Homepage renders new-updates-section, vacancy-0, new-update-0 — OK, no PushSubscribeButton console errors (only two unrelated 401 resource errors + a 'Error 4: S... is not valid JSON' pageerror from another script). (2) The test browser reports Notification.permission='denied' natively and context.grant_permissions(['notifications']) does NOT change it, so the real granted-upfront case must be simulated by stubbing window.Notification via add_init_script. (3) Stubbed granted: requestPermission invoked, button replaced by [data-testid=push-subscribe-status] 'Push Alerts ON ✓' within ~1.5s — but toast text is the catch-block error toast (bug above). (4) Stubbed denied: error toast 'Aapne notifications block kar diye...' and label becomes 'Push Blocked — Settings देखें'; second click shows the lock-icon guidance toast. Button clickable with normal (non-forced) clicks, no overlay issues.
rca_of_the_issue: Original 'button does nothing' bug is fixed — Notification.requestPermission() is now called directly and state/labels update. Residual defect: inside subscribe(), after a successful grant, the code calls window.webpushr('subscribe'); the Webpushr loader stub exists (typeof function) but is uninitialised due to the placeholder site key, so the call throws TypeError. Because it sits above toast.success() in the same try block, control jumps to catch and the error toast is displayed even though permission was granted.
